sentences.text: In kidney podocyte cells, high glucose conditions triggered an increase in the protein EIF4A3 and the circular RNA circ_0000285, which bound together to halt cell growth while promoting death, inflammation, and oxidative stress.

Because the protein Cyclin F, which attaches to EIF4A3 to facilitate its breakdown, decreased under high glucose exposure, researchers found that adding extra Cyclin F reduced inflammation, lowered oxidative stress, and improved kidney function in both living animals and cells.

The authors suggest that the Cyclin F pathway could be a future target for treating diabetic kidney disease, noting that reducing EIF4A3 levels partially fixed the problems caused by high glucose in the cells.
